messages.content: Calculus is the branch of mathematics that studies continuous change and its rate at which it occurs. It was invented primarily by Isaac Newton and Gottfried Leibniz to solve real-world problems, including physics (like motion) and economics (like optimization). In essence, calculus involves two main operations: differentiation to find instantaneous rates or slopes, and integration to calculate accumulation areas like total distance traveled.
